sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic fragment conservativity: temporal cell at Base
sapience_notes.value: The edge from the temporal cell (Until/Since, no box) into TM at FrameClass.Base is false: BimodalLib.not_conservativeEdge_temporal_base. TM derives NF, X-top implies G X-top, from NB (X-top implies box X-top), MF and T; the temporal cell at Base is sound for every linear order without endpoints, and NF fails on the integers followed by the rationals. So filing a temporal statement at its smallest fragment is a convention at Base, not a theorem.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic fragment conservativity: method
sapience_notes.value: Edges are proved by a syntactic translation and one induction on derivations (conservative_of_translation), not by soundness, a semantic bridge and completeness of the smaller logic. A fragment logic is a set of TM derivations, and no completeness theorem in the tree returns a derivation inside a fragment. The Boolean and box edges collapse Until/Since to g-and-e (dense reading) or to e (discrete reading, at ZTime only), keeping box or reading it as identity; no S5 or Burgess-Xu completeness is needed.

sapience_notes.subject: Kalmar completeness in a Prop-valued Hilbert calculus (Lean 4)
sapience_notes.value: Two choices made Kalmar completeness inside an arbitrary sublanguage a 236-line file that compiled first try: (1) state the deduction theorem over any context included in A :: Gamma, so the weakening rule is an instance of the induction hypothesis and no well-founded recursion is needed; (2) take the truth assignment for a context to be membership in that context, so the Kalmar lemma needs no consistency hypothesis and variable elimination is a plain list induction with case analysis by Peirce.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic registered theorems: proof profile census
sapience_notes.value: Measured by evaluating proofProfile on each of the 190 registered derivations (about 10 s with evalExpr): only 3 have a reference proof that derives a formula outside the cell of the statement, all TemporalBoolean at Base and all through box: ConnectDerived.discretePropagateBwd (NA), discreteSymmFwd (NP), discreteSymmBwd. Every Boolean and ModalBoolean row stays inside its cell. Meta-level whnf of the same terms hits the recursion limit on some rows; evaluation does not.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic open temporal conservativity edges
sapience_notes.value: The edges from the temporal cell into TM at Dense, ZTime, RTime, and a repaired Base edge with uniform discreteness as a hypothesis, are open registered conjectures. The obstruction is not a completeness theorem: the translation reads box as always and needs the S5 laws of always, always-phi implies always-G-phi, and replacement of provable equivalents, each derived inside the temporal cell. The repaired hypothesis needs a past conjunct too, since a hypothesis is not closed under time reflection (the rationals times the naturals, lexicographic, satisfy the future conjunct alone).

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic check-module-invariants C5 and generated INDEX.md
sapience_notes.value: C5 reads any dotted BimodalLib.X in markdown as a module path. A conjecture note or edge reference that names a declaration through a namespace that is not a module (BimodalLib.Edges.foo) makes C5 fail on the generated BimodalLib/INDEX.md. Cite the file path or a declaration under a real module prefix in text that the index prints.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic pre-commit typst-sync gate and Tests/
sapience_notes.value: Adding a .lean file under Tests/ moves tests-file-count and tests-line-count in typst/generated/status.typ, so the pre-commit hook refuses the commit until scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix is run and status.typ is staged. The drift is not limited to files under FormalSystem/.
